text:
maria: Bringing up opal-embed-2 (1536d) on INT8 PTQ for embeddings onboarding. Quick sanity run on MSMARCO holdout — seeing a small but consistent recall drop.

raj: which quantization scheme? per-channel or per-tensor? calibration set size?

maria: PTQ per-tensor symmetric, calib=2k samples from our production-like queries. Command I ran:
```bash
python3 eval_embeddings.py --model opal-embed-2 --quant int8 --calib 2000 --dataset msmarco_holdout --metric recall@10
```

taylor: baseline float32 numbers?

maria: float32 R@10 0.842; int8 R@10 0.812 (~-0.03 absolute). Recall@1 drops more: 0.621 -> 0.587. Silhouette score on cluster eval: float32 0.412 -> int8 0.378.

raj: ok that's notable but not catastrophic. Did you normalize embeddings before/after quant? ops for L2?

maria: I run L2-normalize after model output in the eval harness. I also tried pre-quant scaling (multiply by 128) but results similar.

ana: @maria can you paste a tiny histogram of cosine shift (float32 - int8) between pairs? even a few stats (mean/std/max) helps.

maria: quick stats: cosine_diff mean=0.009, std=0.027, max=0.19. Most shifts tiny, but long tail.

ci-bot: [job link] https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/12987 — eval artifacts uploaded (embeddings + recall matrix).

raj: two hypotheses: 1) quantization noise on top-k directions hurts nearest neighbor rank; 2) calibration set distribution mismatch. Try per-channel quant + 5000 calib from high-freq queries. Also try asymmetric quant to preserve zero bias.

maria: running per-channel asymmetric now. Also re-running with 5k calib. ETA ~20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

taylor: also flip to per-channel PTQ with separate scale for each output vector dimension, and check whether norm variance increased post-quant. If L2 norm variance jumps, it can change nearest neighbor ordering.

maria: latest run results:
- per-channel asymmetric, calib=5k: R@10 0.828; R@1 0.599; silhouette 0.401
- still slightly below float, but delta reduced (R@10 delta -0.014).

ana: nice improvement. Could also try tiny quant-aware calibration: collect activations with dropout off and run minmax per-batch, or run a 128-sample optimizer (min MSE) per-channel.

raj: for production recommendation, we should also compare downstream KPIs: rerank improvement, latency trade-off, and unit cost. If int8 saves >30% cost w/ <2ppt R@10 loss that's likely acceptable.

maria: preliminary perf numbers: float32 p99 latency 28ms, int8 p99 18ms on single GPU instance; cost estimate ~35% lower.

taylor: important to check recall stability across query slices (short vs long queries, multilingual). Can you produce per-slice recall deltas?

maria: added per-slice table: short queries R@10 delta -0.02, long queries -0.05, en vs other: en -0.013, multi -0.04. Long queries impacted more (probably distribution shift).

ana: action items:
- maria: run an expanded holdout (10k) with per-channel asymmetric PTQ + 5k calib and dump cosine distributions (hist, quant error per-dim).
- raj: try QAT prototype on a small checkpoint (1 epoch finetune) to see if model recovers R@1.
- taylor: prepare slice-based dashboards for recall/regression alerts.

maria: will run expanded holdout now and upload artifacts. tagging this thread so we keep notes. :pushpin:

ci-bot: artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-ci/embeds/opal-embed-2/int8/per-channel-5k/ (contains eval csvs + plots)

taylor: thanks — can we gate int8 rollouts behind a regression threshold on recall@1 and recall@10 per-slice? propose 1.5ppt on R@10 and 3ppt on R@1 for canary.

raj: agreed. Also add a monitoring job to compare sample of live queries' neighbor overlaps weekly.

maria: sounds good. wrapping up — I'll post final numbers in ~2 runs. :thumbsup:
